subject: Web Development
title: PHP and the Dynamic Revolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply PHP and the Dynamic Revolution.

hook.text: In 1995, Rasmus Lerdorf created a tool to track visits to his online resume.

buildup.text: That tool evolved into PHP — a language you could embed directly inside HTML.

discovery.text: PHP made dynamic pages easy. Mix code with markup and the server handled the rest.

twist.text: Purists hated PHP's messy design. But it powered WordPress, Facebook, and Wikipedia.

climax.text: By 2010, PHP ran nearly 80% of all websites with server-side code.

punchline.text: A resume tracker became the web's engine.
